cases.title: PUJ Obstruction
cases.scenario: A child is found on prenatal ultrasonography to have hydronephrosis. Later imaging shows a markedly dilated renal pelvis. An older patient with the same condition may present with dull aching renal pain.
cases.ar: طفل ظهر في السونار قبل الولادة عنده hydronephrosis، أو مريض أكبر يشكو من dull aching renal pain مع اتساع واضح في renal pelvis.
questions: What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which investigation is used in equivocal cases?
answer: Diagnosis: Pelvi-ureteric junction obstruction (PUJO).
Causes: congenital muscular-development defect; atresia at PUJ; external compression by an aberrant crossing vessel to the lower pole.
US and urography: hydronephrosis with markedly dilated renal pelvis.
CT demonstrates hydronephrosis.
Diuretic renography is used in equivocal cases to verify obstruction.
Treatment: excision of the adynamic PUJ segment and re-anastomosis of the healthy upper ureter to the renal pelvis.
cases.trap: Do not write “hydronephrosis” as the final diagnosis; it is the radiological result. The diagnosis is PUJO.

cases.title: Ectopic Ureteral Orifice
cases.scenario: A female child passes urine normally but has continuous urinary dribbling between normal acts of voiding.
cases.ar: طفلة تتبول بصورة طبيعية، لكن يوجد تنقيط بول مستمر بين مرات التبول.
questions: What is the most likely diagnosis?
Mention possible ectopic sites in males and females.
Mention important associations and the male presentation.
answer: Diagnosis: ectopic ureteral orifice.
The opening is distal to the external urethral sphincter or in the vagina, so urine from the ectopic ureter bypasses continence while the bladder still empties normally.
Male: mostly urethra. Female: urethra or vagina.
Common associations: ureterocele and duplex system. Males may present with epididymo-orchitis.
Asymptomatic: no treatment. Symptomatic: ureterovesical reimplantation.
cases.trap: Continuous dribbling with normal voiding is not ordinary incontinence; it is the pathognomonic history emphasized in the lecture.
cases.memory: Normal voiding + continuous dribbling in a girl = ectopic ureter.

cases.title: Posterior Urethral Valve (PUV)
cases.scenario: Antenatal ultrasound shows a thick-walled trabeculated bladder and an elongated dilated posterior urethra producing a keyhole appearance.
cases.ar: السونار يظهر thick trabeculated bladder مع dilated posterior urethra وعلامة keyhole.
questions: What is the best diagnostic imaging and how should it be performed?
Mention an important associated finding and treatment.
answer: Diagnosis: posterior urethral valve.
An obstructing membrane in the posterior urethra causing obstructive uropathy.
US: thick-walled trabeculated bladder; elongated and dilated posterior urethra; keyhole sign.
Best imaging: MCUG during the micturition phase using lateral or oblique views.
MCUG shows dilatation and elongation of posterior urethra and the valves. Vesicoureteral reflux occurs in 50%.
Treatment: endoscopic valve ablation.
cases.trap: Keyhole sign is an ultrasound clue; MCUG is the best diagnostic imaging technique.
cases.memory: PUV: Keyhole on US → MCUG during micturition → endoscopic ablation.

cases.title: Bladder Exstrophy
cases.scenario: A newborn has an infra-umbilical reddish moist “strawberry” mass. Pelvic X-ray shows wide separation of the symphysis pubis.
cases.ar: مولود لديه كتلة حمراء رطبة أسفل السرة، والأشعة تظهر wide separation of symphysis pubis.
questions: List the clinical findings and genital associations.
answer: Diagnosis: bladder exstrophy.
Incomplete development of the infra-umbilical abdominal wall and incomplete/absent anterior bladder wall.
Clinical: exposed reddish strawberry bladder mass; anterior sub-umbilical wall defect; absent anterior bladder wall; widened symphysis pubis.
Associated: epispadias in males and bifid clitoris in females.
Refer to a highly specialized pediatric urology center. Successful initial closure is the most important factor for good long-term outcome. First stage may be done within 48 hours.
cases.trap: The “strawberry mass” is exposed bladder mucosa, not a tumor.
cases.memory: Exstrophy = strawberry bladder + wide pubic symphysis.

cases.title: Hypospadias
cases.scenario: A male newborn has the urethral meatus on the ventral surface of the penis with ventral curvature and deficient ventral prepuce.
cases.ar: مولود ذكر فتحة البول عنده في السطح السفلي للقضيب مع chordee وdeficient ventral prepuce.
questions: What is the diagnosis and definition?
Mention the types shown in the lecture.
What is the significance of associated undescended testis?
Mention complications, treatment, and an important precaution.
answer: Diagnosis: hypospadias — urethral meatus opens on the ventral side instead of the tip of the glans.
Types: anterior and posterior hypospadias.
Associated: deficient ventral prepuce, chordee, meatal stenosis.
Hypospadias + undescended testis may indicate DSD/ambiguous genitalia: immediate genetic and endocrine work-up after birth to exclude congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
Complications: obstructive uropathy from meatal stenosis, psychological problems, sexual and fertility problems due to chordee.
Treatment: surgical repair. Do not circumcise before repair because the prepuce may be used.
cases.trap: Never forget “Do not circumcise before repair.” It is a classic exam point.

cases.title: Ureterocele + Duplex System
cases.scenario: A cystogram shows a double-walled filling defect at the ureteric orifice with cobra-head appearance. Imaging also demonstrates two renal moieties with two ureters.
cases.ar: الـcystogram يظهر double-walled filling defect بشكل cobra head، مع complete duplex system.
questions: Identify the filling defect and define it.
Describe the typical drainage of the upper-pole ureter and common associations.
answer: The filling defect is a ureterocele: cystic dilatation of the terminal ureter projecting into the bladder and/or urethra.
Diagnosis: ultrasound; cystogram may show double-walled filling defect/cobra-head appearance.
Treatment: endoscopic incision of the ureterocele wall.
Complete duplex system: two renal moieties with two ureters.
The upper-pole ureter may drain ectopically, e.g. into the urethra in a female, while the other opens normally into the bladder.
Common associations: ectopic ureter and ureterocele; ureterocele may produce obstruction and hydroureter.
cases.trap: Cobra-head appearance belongs to ureterocele, not ectopic ureter itself.
cases.memory: Ureterocele = terminal cystic dilatation + cobra head.

cases.title: Horseshoe Kidney
cases.scenario: Imaging for recurrent urinary infection or stones shows both kidneys at a lower level than normal with fusion of the lower poles.
cases.ar: التصوير يظهر الكليتين في مستوى أقل من الطبيعي مع التحام القطبين السفليين.
answer: Diagnosis: horseshoe kidney.
The lower poles of both kidneys are fused by an isthmus, which may be fibrous or parenchymal.
May be asymptomatic. Complications: UTI and stone formation.
Diagnosis: palpable abdominal mass, US, CT, IVU; kidneys lie at a lower level and lower poles are fused.
No treatment unless complicated, mostly by stone disease.
cases.trap: The lecture specifically states fusion of the lower poles.
cases.memory: Horseshoe kidney → lower poles fused by an isthmus.

cases.title: Cryptorchidism
cases.scenario: A child has an empty hemiscrotum. The testis may be palpable in the groin or completely impalpable.
cases.ar: طفل لديه empty hemiscrotum، والخصية قد تكون palpable في groin أو impalpable.
questions: How should the child be examined?
Differentiate retractile from true undescended testis.
State timing and method of treatment and management of impalpable testis.
answer: Cryptorchidism means hidden/undescended testis not present normally in the scrotum.
Palpable: retractile, undescended, ectopic. Ectopic sites: superficial inguinal pouch (most common), base of penis, perineum, femoral canal.
Impalpable: intra-abdominal, inguinal but atrophic, absent/vanishing.
Examination: warm hands; examine scrotum and inguinal canal in supine, frog-leg and squatting positions.
Retractile testis can be brought to bottom of scrotum and requires no treatment.
Complications: infertility from thermal effect, trauma, tumor especially intra-abdominal, torsion.

If no descent by 6 months it will probably remain undescended. Orchiopexy before 1.5 years; fixation in sub-dartos pouch and herniotomy for associated sac. Impalpable testis: laparoscopy for diagnosis and possible treatment in the same session.
cases.trap: Retractile testis is not a true undescended testis and requires no treatment.
cases.memory: No descent by 6 months → likely persistent; orchiopexy before 1.5 years.

cases.title: Anomalies of Renal Number
cases.scenario: A CT shows two kidneys in the right lumbar region with partial fusion and one kidney on the left side.
cases.ar: الـCT يظهر كليتين في الناحية اليمنى مع partial fusion وكلية في اليسار.
questions: Compare bilateral and unilateral renal agenesis.
State typical features of a supernumerary kidney.
answer: The image suggests a supernumerary kidney.
Bilateral agenesis: extremely rare and incompatible with life.
Unilateral agenesis: opposite kidney undergoes compensatory hypertrophy to maintain excretory function.
Supernumerary kidney: rare, most commonly left-sided and caudal to the normal kidney.
cases.trap: Do not mislabel the lecture CT as unilateral agenesis; it demonstrates a supernumerary kidney configuration.
cases.memory: Supernumerary kidney: rare, usually left and caudal.

cases.title: Ectopic Kidney
cases.scenario: One kidney is seen above the diaphragm in one patient; another kidney remains in the pelvis and is small and malrotated.
cases.ar: حالة فيها الكلية فوق الحجاب الحاجز، وحالة أخرى الكلية بقيت في الحوض وكانت small and malrotated.
questions: Explain the developmental basis of each.
Mention the typical features of a pelvic kidney.
answer: Thoracic kidney: excessive ascent above the diaphragm.
Pelvic kidney: failure of ascent to the normal flank position.
Pelvic kidney is often small and malrotated.
cases.trap: Thoracic kidney is an anomaly of excessive ascent; pelvic kidney is failure of ascent.
cases.memory: Thoracic = above diaphragm; pelvic = failed ascent.

cases.title: Hypospadias vs Epispadias
cases.scenario: Two newborns have abnormal urethral openings: one on the ventral side and the other on the dorsal side of the penis.
cases.ar: مولودان: فتحة البول عند الأول ventral وعند الثاني dorsal.
questions: Mention the key management precaution in hypospadias.
answer: Ventral opening: hypospadias. Dorsal opening: epispadias.
Epispadias is a rare congenital defect with the urethral meatus on the dorsal aspect instead of the tip of the glans.
Do not circumcise a child with hypospadias before repair because the prepuce may be needed.
cases.memory: HYPO is under/ventral; EPI is over/dorsal.

Diagnosis: palpable abdominal mass, US, CT or IVU; both kidneys lie lower than normal and the lower poles are fused.
Treatment: no treatment unless complicated, especially by stone disease.

coreShorts.q: Enumerate the causes of pelvi-ureteric junction obstruction (PUJO).
a: Congenital defect in muscular development.
Atresia at the PUJ.
External compression by an aberrant crossing vessel to the lower pole.

coreShorts.q: Outline the surgical treatment of PUJO.

Re-anastomosis of the healthy upper end of the ureter to the renal pelvis.

coreShorts.q: Define ectopic ureteral orifice and mention its common sites in males and females.
a: Definition: a ureter terminates at an abnormal site.
Male: mostly in the urethra.
Female: in the urethra or vagina.
It is commonly associated with ureterocele and duplex system.

a: Male presentation: epididymo-orchitis.
Female pathognomonic history: continuous urinary dribbling despite normal voiding when the opening is distal to the external sphincter or in the vagina.
Asymptomatic: no treatment.

coreShorts.q: Write a short note on ureterocele.
a: Definition: cystic dilatation of the terminal ureter projecting into the bladder and/or urethra.
Diagnosis: ultrasound; cystogram may show a double-walled filling defect with cobra-head appearance.

coreShorts.q: Describe the complete duplex system shown in the lecture and state the drainage of the upper-pole ureter.
a: A complete duplex system has two renal moieties with two ureters.
The upper-pole ureter may drain ectopically, for example into the female urethra.
The other ureter opens normally into the bladder.
It is commonly associated with ectopic ureter and ureterocele.

coreShorts.q: Define bladder exstrophy and describe its clinical picture and associated abnormalities.
a: Rare congenital anomaly with incomplete development of the infra-umbilical abdominal wall and anterior bladder wall.
The bladder protrudes as an infra-umbilical reddish moist strawberry mass.
Anterior sub-umbilical wall defect and absent anterior bladder wall.
Epispadias in males, bifid clitoris in females, and widened symphysis pubis.

Successful initial closure is the most important factor for a good long-term result.
The first stage of repair may be performed within 48 hours.

coreShorts.q: Define posterior urethral valve (PUV) and list its ultrasound findings.
a: Definition: an obstructing membrane in the posterior urethra causing obstructive uropathy.
US: thick-walled trabeculated bladder.
Elongated and dilated posterior urethra.
Keyhole sign.

coreShorts.q: What is the best imaging technique for PUV, how is it performed, and what does it show?
a: Best imaging: micturating cystourethrogram (MCUG).
Performed during the micturition phase using lateral or oblique views.
Shows dilatation and elongation of the posterior urethra and the posterior urethral valves.

coreShorts.q: State the important associated finding and treatment of PUV.
a: Vesicoureteral reflux is seen in 50% of patients according to the lecture.

coreShorts.q: Define hypospadias, mention its types, and list associated abnormalities.
a: Definition: urethral meatus opens on the ventral side of the penis instead of the tip of the glans.
Types shown: anterior and posterior hypospadias.
Associated abnormalities: deficient ventral prepuce, chordee, and meatal stenosis.

coreShorts.q: What is the significance of hypospadias associated with an undescended testis?
a: It may indicate a disorder of sexual differentiation or ambiguous genitalia.
An immediate genetic and endocrine work-up is required after birth.
Congenital adrenal hyperplasia must be excluded.

coreShorts.q: Enumerate the complications of hypospadias and state its treatment and essential precaution.
a: Obstructive uropathy due to meatal stenosis.
Psychological problems.
Sexual and fertility problems due to chordee.
Treatment: surgical repair.
Do not circumcise before repair because the prepuce may be used.

coreShorts.q: Define epispadias and differentiate it from hypospadias.
a: Epispadias: urethral meatus opens on the dorsal aspect of the penis instead of the tip of the glans.
Hypospadias: ventral opening.
Epispadias: dorsal opening.

coreShorts.q: Define cryptorchidism and classify maldescended testes.
a: Cryptorchidism means a hidden/undescended testis not normally present in the scrotum; incidence in the lecture is 3%.
Palpable: retractile, true undescended, and ectopic testis.
Impalpable: intra-abdominal, inguinal but atrophic, and absent/vanishing testis.

coreShorts.q: Differentiate retractile, true undescended, and ectopic testis.
a: Retractile: due to an overactive cremasteric reflex; can be brought to the bottom of the scrotum by squatting in a warm room; no treatment.
True undescended: arrested along the normal path from retroperitoneum to scrotum.
Ectopic: completed descent but lies in an abnormal site; superficial inguinal pouch is the most common site.

coreShorts.q: Describe the clinical examination of a child with an empty scrotum.
a: Warm the hands.
Examine the scrotum and inguinal canal.
Examine in supine, frog-leg, and squatting positions.
A retractile testis can be moved by hand from the groin into the scrotum.

coreShorts.q: Enumerate the complications of undescended testis.
a: Infertility due to the thermal effect.
Trauma.
Tumor, especially in an intra-abdominal testis.
Torsion.

coreShorts.q: Outline the treatment of undescended and impalpable testes, including the important timing points.
a: Retractile testis: no treatment.
If the testis has not descended by 6 months, it will probably remain undescended.
Early orchiopexy is recommended before 1.5 years.
Fix the testis in a scrotal sub-dartos pouch and perform herniotomy if an associated hernia sac is present.
Impalpable testis: laparoscopy for diagnosis and possible treatment in the same session.

detailedShorts.a: Obstructive uropathy due to meatal stenosis, psychological problems, and sexual or fertility problems due to chordee.

detailedShorts.q: State the treatment of hypospadias and the essential preoperative precaution.
detailedShorts.a: Surgical repair; do not circumcise before repair because the prepuce may be used in reconstruction.

detailedShorts.q: Define epispadias.
detailedShorts.a: A rare congenital defect in which the urethral meatus opens on the dorsal aspect of the penis instead of the tip of the glans.

detailedShorts.q: Differentiate hypospadias from epispadias.
detailedShorts.a: Hypospadias has a ventral urethral opening; epispadias has a dorsal urethral opening.

detailedShorts.q: Define cryptorchidism and state its incidence.
detailedShorts.a: Cryptorchidism is an undescended or hidden testis not present in the scrotum; the incidence is 3% in the lecture.

detailedShorts.q: Mention the possible etiological factors of undescended testis.
detailedShorts.a: The cause is unknown but may involve mechanical factors or gonadotrophic hormone deficiency.

detailedShorts.q: Classify palpable maldescended testes.
detailedShorts.a: Retractile testis, true undescended testis, and ectopic testis.

detailedShorts.q: Enumerate the sites of ectopic testis.
detailedShorts.a: Superficial inguinal pouch (most common), base of the penis or pubic region, perineum, and femoral canal.

detailedShorts.q: Classify impalpable testes.
detailedShorts.a: Intra-abdominal testis, inguinal but atrophic testis, and absent or vanishing testis.

detailedShorts.q: Describe the clinical examination of a child with an empty scrotum.
detailedShorts.a: Warm the hands; examine the scrotum and inguinal canal; assess in supine, frog-leg, and squatting positions.

detailedShorts.q: Describe retractile testis and state its treatment.
detailedShorts.a: It results from an overactive cremasteric reflex, can be brought to the bottom of the scrotum in a warm room or by squatting, and requires no treatment.

detailedShorts.q: Enumerate the complications of undescended testis.
detailedShorts.a: Infertility from thermal effect, trauma, tumor especially in intra-abdominal testes, and torsion.

detailedShorts.q: State the important timing points in treatment of undescended testis.
detailedShorts.a: If it has not descended by 6 months it will probably remain undescended; early surgical treatment is recommended before 1.5 years.

detailedShorts.q: Outline orchiopexy as described in the lecture.
detailedShorts.a: Fix the testis in a scrotal sub-dartos pouch and perform herniotomy if an associated hernia sac is present.

detailedShorts.q: How is an impalpable testis managed?
detailedShorts.a: Laparoscopy is used as a diagnostic tool and may allow treatment in the same session.
